plain.li: [festival] I hope they drink to us at {GOD}'s feast.
[festival] Our gift is on its way to {GOD}'s table.
[sacrilege] {KILLER} shouldn't have touched that one, it was {GOD}'s.
[sacrilege] That beast was sacred to {GOD}, and {GOD} will have noticed.
[sacrilege,real:felt] Some say {GOD} keeps count of every one of those.
[beasts] They came straight for me, as if someone sent them.
[beasts] {GOD} hasn't forgotten, has {GOD}?
[beasts,real:felt] Wolves, out of nowhere, and some say I know why.
[blight] The crop's rotting where it stands, and you know whose anger that is.
[blight] We slighted {GOD}, and now look at the fields.
[blight,real:believed] Blight's blight, but I'd still leave {GOD} a sheaf next year.
[blight,real:felt] Some say it's {GOD}, and some say it's the damp.
[eclipse] The sun's gone out at noon, and I don't like it one bit.
[eclipse] {GOD} has turned away from us, and taken the light.
[eclipse,real:felt] It's only the moon in the way, surely.
[lightning] That bolt had a name on it.
[lightning] {GOD} is shouting at someone tonight.
[lightning] Right on {OFFENDER}'s roof, and you tell me that's chance.
[lightning,real:felt] Some say the storm picks its roofs.
[blessing] The fever's broken, and I'm not asking who broke it.
[blessing] Thank {GOD} for that, I thought we'd lose them.
[blessing,real:felt] Some say {GOD} sat with them in the night.
[blessing,real:believed] Good care and a strong heart did that, mostly.
[champion] {GOD} is with me today.
[champion] Stand aside, I fight for {GOD}.
[champfell] Their champion's down, and {GOD} saw it.
[champfell] So much for {GOD}'s chosen.
[champfell,real:felt] Some say that's a sign, and I say so too.
[gift] {GIFTED} has been touched by {GOD}, you can see it.
[gift] I felt the air change when {GOD}'s gift came down.
[gift,real:felt] Some say it's {GOD}'s gift, and {GIFTED} isn't arguing.
[trickcurse] Everything I touch goes wrong now, and somebody's laughing.
[trickcurse] I should have known better than to take {GOD}'s gift.
[trickback] It's come back to me, whatever it was.
[trickback] {GOD} has had the joke, and I've got the gift again.
[hunger] It always takes more, they say.
[hunger] I can feel where it took from them, like a cold draught.
[hunger] Don't answer it next time, whatever it offers.
[quarrelstorm] {GOD} has the sky today.
[quarrelstorm] Here's {GOD}'s answer, in thunder.
[quarrelstorm,real:felt] Some say the gods are fighting, and some say it's spring.
[quarreldry] Not a cloud, so {GOD} has won the day.
[quarreldry] {GOD} is holding the rain back out of spite.
[side] We've picked a side, and I hope it was the right one.
[side] {GOD} will remember we stood with them.
[deadmark] There's an old god's sign cut into this, worn nearly smooth.
[deadmark] Somebody prayed to {GOD} here, long before us.
[fading] Say the old name once, it costs nothing.
[fading] {GOD} has nobody left, so let it have us for a night.
[newborn] Our little god is growing.
[newborn] I could swear {GOD} answered me.
[newborn,child] Is {GOD} our god, just ours?
They say {MYTHGOD} and {MYTHOTHER} quarrelled first, and nobody knows why.
{MYTHGOD} and {MYTHOTHER} shared one cup at the world's first feast.
[myth:rivals] {MYTHGOD} and {MYTHOTHER} hated each other before the sky was made.
[myth:rivals,myth:0] {MYTHGOD} once stole the rain from {MYTHOTHER}'s fields.
[myth:rivals,myth:1] This weather is {MYTHGOD} and {MYTHOTHER} at it again.
[myth:rivals,myth:2] {MYTHGOD} won the last round, and {MYTHOTHER} is sulking.
[myth:rivals,god:storm,other:harvest] {MYTHGOD} keeps the rain to spite {MYTHOTHER}.
[myth:lovers] {MYTHGOD} met {MYTHOTHER} at a crossroads, and neither stepped aside.
[myth:lovers,myth:0] {MYTHGOD} courted {MYTHOTHER} for a hundred years.
[myth:lovers,myth:2] {MYTHGOD} and {MYTHOTHER} have made it up again, they say.
[myth:estranged] {MYTHGOD} and {MYTHOTHER} were lovers once, and now never speak.
[myth:estranged,myth:1] {MYTHGOD} walked out on {MYTHOTHER} in the middle of a storm.
[myth:parent] {MYTHOTHER} was born of {MYTHGOD} out of a single spark.
[myth:parent,myth:1] {MYTHOTHER} still lives in {MYTHGOD}'s shadow, and hates it.
[myth:siblings] {MYTHGOD} and {MYTHOTHER} are sister and brother, and bicker like it.
[myth:siblings,myth:0] {MYTHGOD} and {MYTHOTHER} cut the world in two with a knife.
[myth:twins] {MYTHGOD} and {MYTHOTHER} are twins, and nobody knows which one answers.
[myth:twins,myth:1] The twins fight over every soul, {MYTHGOD} pulling and {MYTHOTHER} pushing.
[myth:allies] {MYTHGOD} and {MYTHOTHER} shook hands at the world's edge.
[myth:allies,myth:2] {MYTHOTHER} still owes {MYTHGOD} for the last favour.
[myth:castdown] {MYTHGOD} threw {MYTHOTHER} out of the sky, and it was never forgiven.
[myth:castdown,myth:0] {MYTHOTHER} was great once, until {MYTHGOD} took the throne.
[myth:stolepeople] {MYTHGOD} stole {MYTHOTHER}'s people away with better promises.
[myth:stolepeople,myth:1] {MYTHOTHER}'s old faithful pray to {MYTHGOD} now.
[godkey:stormfather] The thunder is {MYTHGOD} checking the chain on the deep vault.
[godkey:ferryman] {MYTHGOD} once ferried a man who wasn't dead yet, and charges double since.
[godkey:green] {MYTHGOD} remembers every axe, and every tree that fell to one.
